faqs.question: When is Propose Day 2027?
faqs.answer: Propose Day 2027 is Monday 8 February. It is the second day of Valentine week, after Rose Day on Sunday 7 February, and Valentine's Day closes the week on Sunday 14 February.

faqs.question: Should I write my line with ನೀನು or ನೀವು?
faqs.answer: Use ನೀನು if the person already says ನೀನು to you, and ನೀವು for anyone older, anyone met through family, and any situation where you are asking rather than confirming. The verb ending has to follow: -ಉತ್ತೀ with ನೀನು, -ಉತ್ತೀರಿ with ನೀವು.

faqs.question: How do you say I love you in Kannada?
faqs.answer: ನಾನು ನಿನ್ನನ್ನು ಪ್ರೀತಿಸುತ್ತೇನೆ (nānu ninnannu prītisuttēne). Kittel's dictionary glosses ಪ್ರೀತಿಸು as to love, with accusative, which is why the object is ನಿನ್ನನ್ನು rather than ನಿನ್ನ.

faqs.question: What is will you marry me in Kannada?
faqs.answer: ನೀನು ನನ್ನನ್ನು ಮದುವೆಯಾಗುತ್ತೀ? to someone you are close to, and ನೀವು ನನ್ನನ್ನು ಮದುವೆಯಾಗುತ್ತೀರಿ? as the respectful form. The only difference is the verb ending, and it has to match the pronoun.

faqs.question: Why are there only twelve lines here?
faqs.answer: Nineteen were drafted and seven were cut because a word or an ending could not be verified against Kittel's dictionary. A wrong line inside a proposal is worse than a shorter page, so the cuts stayed cut.

faqs.question: Did a native Kannada speaker check these lines?
faqs.answer: No. Every word and every ending was checked against a published dictionary and a published grammar, both fetched and read, but no native speaker reviewed the page. If you have one to hand, read the line to them before you send it.

faqs.question: What does the -ಉತ್ತೀರಿ ending actually do?
faqs.answer: It marks the second person plural of the present, and Kannada uses that plural to one person as a mark of respect. Kittel's dictionary lists it as the plural of the singular -ಈ ending, with ಹೋಗುತ್ತೀರಿ and ಇರುತ್ತೀರಿ as examples.

faqs.question: Is ಕೈ ಹಿಡಿ a proposal or just holding hands?
faqs.answer: Both, and that is the point of it. ಹಿಡಿ is glossed as to seize, to take, and ಕೈ ಹಿಡಿ carries the marriage sense alongside the literal one, so it is not a low-stakes line.

faqs.question: Why do the dictionary spellings look different from the lines?
faqs.answer: Kittel writes a nasal before a stop as a conjunct, so ತುಮ್ಬಾ where modern Kannada writes ತುಂಬಾ with anusvara. The lines on this page use modern orthography; the dictionary entries behind them use the older convention.

faqs.question: Can I put a Kannada line on a SubhSandesh page?
faqs.answer: Yes, the text you type is kept exactly as you type it. The templates themselves are English-language though, so every label and button around your Kannada line will be in English.

faqs.question: What if I am not proposing marriage at all?
faqs.answer: Most Propose Day searching is not about marriage. Use the two dative ಇಷ್ಟ lines, which have no verb to conjugate, and send them on an I-love-you page rather than a proposal page.

faqs.question: Does the line have to be sent on Propose Day itself?
faqs.answer: No, and building it earlier is easier. The median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is 2.4 hours, sampled on /apology-dashboard with n=1,348, so giving yourself an evening rather than a lunch break is realistic.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Propose Day Quotes in Kannada, With the Register Marked

Propose Day 2027 falls on Monday 8 February, the second day of Valentine week — Rose Day is Sunday 7 February and Valentine's Day is Sunday 14 February. Below are twelve Kannada lines, each in ಕನ್ನಡ script with a Roman transliteration and an English gloss, and each marked for register: ನೀನು (nīnu) for someone you are already close to, ನೀವು (nīvu) for someone you are not.

Nineteen lines were drafted and seven were cut, because every word was checked against a dictionary before it went on the page. If you would rather send the line as a page than as a message, SubhSandesh has recorded 5,061 personalised pages created since 12 March 2026 across 20 page types, and 38.7% of those creators password-protect the page before they share the link.

Both figures are platform-wide across all 20 page types, not proposal figures — no proposal-specific data exists for this site.

## What ನೀನು and ನೀವು change in a Kannada line

Kannada has two second-person pronouns and they are not interchangeable. ನೀನು (nīnu) is the singular and ನೀವು (nīvu) is its plural, and the plural is what you use to one person when you mean respect.

The choice is not a politeness word you can bolt on or drop. It commits the verb for the rest of the sentence. [Kittel's Kannada–English dictionary](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/dictionaries/kittel/) lists the two endings as separate entries: -ಈ is "an affix for the second person singular of the common present", with ಮಾಡುತ್ತೀ "thou doest" as its example, and -ಈರಿ is "the plural of -ಈ", with ಹೋಗುತ್ತೀರಿ and ಇರುತ್ತೀರಿ.

So ನೀನು … ಹಿಡಿಯುತ್ತೀ and ನೀವು … ಹಿಡಿಯುತ್ತೀರಿ are the same question asked of two different relationships. Mixing the halves is the error a Kannada reader catches in the first second.

[Kittel's 1903 grammar](https://archive.org/details/grammarofkannada00kittuoft) states the social rule in §258: "when addressing a person of some respectability, the plural ನೀವು (also in its oblique cases) is always used, followed by a verb in the plural; and when addressing a person of low rank, or a child, the singular ನೀನು is always used."

That sentence is 123 years old and its social scale reads badly now. What survives intact is the grammar: ನೀವು takes a plural verb, ನೀನು takes a singular one. The same dictionary records a third device — an honorific suffix -ಇರಿ, "generally added to the end of any final word which is employed in addressing a superior or a dear person".

## Twelve propose day quotes in Kannada, grouped by who you are asking

### 1. Three lines for someone you are already close to

**Register.** ನೀನು throughout. These are lines for a partner, not for a first approach.

**The lines.**
ನಾನು ನಿನ್ನನ್ನು ಪ್ರೀತಿಸುತ್ತೇನೆ. — *nānu ninnannu prītisuttēne* — "I love you."
ನೀನು ನನ್ನ ಜೊತೆ ಇದ್ದರೆ ಸಾಕು. — *nīnu nanna jote iddare sāku* — "It is enough if you are with me."
ನಿನ್ನ ನಗೆ ನನಗೆ ಇಷ್ಟ. — *ninna nage nanage iṣṭa* — "I like your laugh."

**Who it suits.** Someone who already says ನೀನು back to you. ಪ್ರೀತಿಸು is glossed in Kittel as "to love (with accusative)", which is why the object is ನಿನ್ನನ್ನು and not ನಿನ್ನ.

**When not to use it.** Not to someone older, and not to a person you are meeting through family.

### 2. The two asks, in ನೀನು

**Register.** ನೀನು with the second-person singular present ending -ಉತ್ತೀ.

**The lines.**
ನೀನು ನನ್ನ ಕೈ ಹಿಡಿಯುತ್ತೀ? — *nīnu nanna kai hiḍiyuttī?* — "Will you take my hand?"
ನೀನು ನನ್ನನ್ನು ಮದುವೆಯಾಗುತ್ತೀ? — *nīnu nannannu maduveyāguttī?* — "Will you marry me?"

**Who it suits.** A couple already together, where the open question is when rather than whether.

**When not to use it.** ಕೈ ಹಿಡಿ carries the marriage sense as well as the literal one, so it is not a soft opener. If you only mean that you want to hold their hand, leave the Kannada out of it.

### 3. The same two asks, in ನೀವು

**Register.** ನೀವು with the plural present ending -ಉತ್ತೀರಿ, and the genitive ನಿಮ್ಮ rather than ನಿನ್ನ.

**The lines.**
ನೀವು ನನ್ನ ಕೈ ಹಿಡಿಯುತ್ತೀರಿ? — *nīvu nanna kai hiḍiyuttīri?* — "Will you take my hand?"
ನೀವು ನನ್ನನ್ನು ಮದುವೆಯಾಗುತ್ತೀರಿ? — *nīvu nannannu maduveyāguttīri?* — "Will you marry me?"
ನೀವು ಒಪ್ಪಿದರೆ ಸಾಕು. — *nīvu oppidare sāku* — "It is enough if you consent."
ನಿಮ್ಮ ಉತ್ತರಕ್ಕೆ ಕಾಯುತ್ತೇನೆ. — *nimma uttarakke kāyuttēne* — "I am waiting for your answer."
ನೀವೇ ನನ್ನ ಸಂಗಾತಿ. — *nīvē nanna saṅgāti* — "You are my companion."

**Who it suits.** An arranged introduction, a colleague, anyone older, and any case where you are genuinely asking rather than confirming.

**When not to use it.** Between two people who already use ನೀನು with each other, switching to ನೀವು reads as a step backwards.

### 4. Two lines that are not a marriage proposal

**Register.** ನೀನು, because these belong to a relationship that already exists.

**The lines.**
ನೀನು ನನಗೆ ತುಂಬಾ ಇಷ್ಟ. — *nīnu nanage tumbā iṣṭa* — "I like you very much."
ನಿನ್ನ ಮಾತು ಕೇಳುವುದು ನನಗೆ ಇಷ್ಟ. — *ninna mātu kēḷuvudu nanage iṣṭa* — "I like listening to you talk."

**Who it suits.** Most Propose Day searching is not about marriage. ಇಷ್ಟ is glossed in Kittel as "wished, desired, agreeable; dear, beloved", and the construction is dative, so there is no verb to conjugate and no register trap.

**When not to use it.** Do not send these expecting them to read as an engagement. In Kannada they are not close to one.

Once you have a line worth sending, the [Will You Marry Me? proposal scrapbook](/proposal) builds your story into a page ending on a YES button that grows every time they dodge it.

## How each line was checked, and which seven were cut

Nineteen lines were drafted, twelve published, seven cut. Every content word in a published line has a headword in Kittel's dictionary, hosted by the Digital Dictionaries of South Asia at the University of Chicago, and every inflection maps to an affix that dictionary lists with worked examples.

The cuts, with reasons. ಬರಿದು, wanted for "empty", returned no headword. ಇದ್ದೀಯ, a modern colloquial second-person form, is not among the second-person affixes the dictionary lists. ಉಳಿ, wanted for "to remain", is entered as "to conceal oneself", "a chisel" and "a thief".

ಬಾಳು is entered first as "a knife, a sword", which is not what you want inside a proposal. ಮರೆ, wanted for "to forget", is entered as "a kind of deer". ಯಾವಾಗಲೂ, "always", returned no headword. And the infinitive ಕಳೆಯಲು returned nothing at all.

Register agreement was checked the same way: every ನೀವು line takes -ಉತ್ತೀರಿ or a verb with no person marking. The colloquial question particle -ಯಾ, as in ಮದುವೆಯಾಗುತ್ತೀಯಾ, could not be attested, so no line here uses it — the two questions rely on intonation, which the dictionary does attest.

That method has a real limit. A dictionary of 1894, revised 1968–71, is good evidence that a word exists and means what is claimed. It is not evidence that a line sounds natural in Bengaluru this February. **No native Kannada speaker reviewed these lines.**

## Where each group of lines belongs

Each group differs by who is being asked, which fixes the pronoun and then the ending. The page-type figures below are platform-wide across all 20 SubhSandesh page types.

| Line group | Pronoun and ending | Who it is for | Nearest page type, and its share of the 5,061 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Already close | ನೀನು, no person ending | A partner you are not proposing to | /love-gf — 1,173 created, 23.2% |
| The ask, intimate | ನೀನು, -ಉತ್ತೀ | A partner you are proposing to | /proposal — outside the top five page types |
| The ask, respectful | ನೀವು, -ಉತ್ತೀರಿ | An introduction, or someone older | /proposal — outside the top five page types |
| Not a proposal | ನೀನು, dative ಇಷ್ಟ | Someone you like and have not asked | /love-gf — 1,173 created, 23.2% |

Pick the row by who is reading, then take the line — not the other way round.

## When a SubhSandesh page is the wrong place for a Kannada line

The templates are English-language, and that is the honest limit here. Your line sits inside the page exactly as you type it, in ಕನ್ನಡ, but every label, button and prompt around it is English. For a grandparent who reads only Kannada, that is one sentence they can read inside a frame they cannot, and a handwritten card beats it.

Two more cases where the page loses. If you are in the same room, say the line out loud. And 48.4% of views across the platform are on a phone — 27,185 of 56,152, again across all 20 page types — so a recipient who will open it on a work laptop is not the reader these pages are built for.

If this is not a marriage proposal, the [romantic "I love you" page for a partner](/love-gf) fits better: second-most created page type at 1,173 pages, 23.2% of everything created, and most-viewed at 16,902 views. Leave time either way — the median gap between first save and last edit is 2.4 hours, sampled on /apology-dashboard, n=1,348. If neither suits, [the full SubhSandesh template list](/templates) is worth a look first.

## Why well-checked Kannada is scarce online

A 2023 paper in the [Journal of Information Technology Management](https://jitm.ut.ac.ir/article_89408.html) built a Kannada syntax parser on a treebank the authors had to generate themselves from 1,000 annotated sentences, tested it on 150 more, and reported 74.2% precision, 79.4% recall and an F1 of 75.3%. A thousand sentences is the working corpus — that is the scale Kannada language tooling is still built at.

There is a quieter reason a line copied off a web page can be wrong while looking right. [The Unicode Standard](https://www.unicode.org/versions/Unicode17.0.0/core-spec/chapter-12/) encodes Kannada at U+0C80–U+0CFF and specifies that vowel letters are atomic: ಊ must be the single code point U+0C8A, not U+0C89 followed by the vowel sign U+0CBE, although the two render identically. Text assembled the wrong way looks correct and breaks on search, sorting and screen readers. Typing the line yourself is safer than pasting one.

## Sources

- Kittel's Kannada–English Dictionary, revised edition, University of Madras, 1968–71, hosted by the Digital Dictionaries of South Asia — https://dsal.uchicago.edu/dictionaries/kittel/
- F. Kittel, *A Grammar of the Kannada Language in English*, Basel Mission, Mangalore, 1903 — https://archive.org/details/grammarofkannada00kittuoft
- Rajani Shree M. and Shambhavi B. R., "Generation of Syntax Parser on South Indian Language using Bottom-Up Parsing Technique and PCFG", *Journal of Information Technology Management*, vol. 15, Special Issue 2023, pp. 19–33 — https://jitm.ut.ac.ir/article_89408.html
- The Unicode Standard, Version 17.0, Chapter 12, §12.8 Kannada — https://www.unicode.org/versions/Unicode17.0.0/core-spec/chapter-12/

structuralLimitations: The Kannada lines were NOT reviewed by a native speaker. Every content word was required to return a headword in Kittel's Kannada-English dictionary (DSAL, University of Chicago) with the sense the line uses, and every inflection was required to map to an affix that dictionary lists as its own entry with worked examples (-ಏನೆ, -ಈ 7, -ಈರಿ 1, -ಇರಿ 3, conditional -ದರೆ, verbal noun -ುವುದು). Register agreement was checked against Kittel's 1903 grammar §258. That establishes that the words and endings exist and mean what the page says; it does not establish that a line sounds natural to a Kannada speaker in 2027. Nineteen lines were drafted, twelve published, seven cut, with the reason for each cut published in the body.

The source dictionary is conservative in two ways that are disclosed on the page. It is a nineteenth-century work (revised edition 1968-71), so its social framing of ನೀನು — "a person of low rank, or a child" — is stated as historical and not endorsed. And its orthography writes a nasal before a stop as a conjunct (ತುಮ್ಬಾ, ನ್ದ) where modern standard Kannada uses anusvara (ತುಂಬಾ, ಂದ); the published lines use modern orthography, which the dictionary entries therefore do not spell identically.

The colloquial interrogative particle -ಯಾ (as in ಮದುವೆಯಾಗುತ್ತೀಯಾ) could not be attested in the dictionary, so no published line uses it; the two question lines rely on intonation, a pattern the dictionary does attest. This is a deliberate conservatism, not a claim that -ಯಾ is wrong.

Several open-access sources that would have improved the page could not be fetched from this machine: tandfonline.com returned 403 on the Cogent Arts & Humanities paper on the Gokak movement and Kannada sub-nationalism; mdpi.com returned 403; degruyterbrill.com returned an empty body; and library.oapen.org, books.openedition.org and hasp.ub.uni-heidelberg.de all served an Anubis bot-challenge, which blocked Zydenbos's open-access A Manual of Modern Kannada — the one modern published grammar that would have corroborated the register section against twentieth-century usage rather than 1903 usage.

Four sources rather than five or six. The PMC family (europepmc.org / pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, counted together) and frontiersin.org were already at the batch's 3-post domain cap and were not used; aclanthology.org, arxiv.org and doi.org were avoided as crowded under the mid-batch source-cap race warning. The four used satisfy the subject test, the peer-reviewed open-access requirement and the generic-context-statistic limit (zero used).

No source URL appears in more than 2 posts in this batch; no domain in more than 3. **One exception: the date/festival reference** (e.g. a panchang for the festival date and muhurat). Every post in a festival batch may verify the same date — that is a fact-check, not a citation, and it has no cap. It only earns a place in `citation` where the post actually states the time; a post that merely mentions the date keeps it out of `sources` and `citation` entirely.

failed.item: H2s map to the fan-out sub-queries identified in Phase 2
failed.why: Phase 2 was run as a cannibalisation and gap analysis against the three sibling language posts, not as a fan-out decomposition, because no SERP for this keyword was measured and no People Also Ask box was seen. The H2s were derived from the register problem and the verification ledger rather than from observed sub-queries, so this item is recorded as failed rather than assumed. Re-run it once an India-served SERP for `propose day quotes in kannada` has actually been measured.

auditReport.honestAssessment: The one thing here that no competing page can copy cheaply is the ನೀನು/ನೀವು register pair printed with the verb ending on both sides and sourced to a named grammar section, plus a published cut ledger — twelve lines kept of nineteen drafted, with the dictionary reason for each of the seven cuts. That is a verifiability claim, not a comprehensiveness claim, and it is the only reason an answer engine would prefer this to a page with forty lines. Against that: no SERP for this keyword was measured in this run, so nothing here is asserted about what currently ranks. Indian-language Propose Day queries run on an annual February news cycle owned by publishers whose domain authority is far above ours, so the realistic target is position 6-10 rather than 3, over months rather than weeks, and the page is a visibility asset judged on impressions — a copy-text query converts close to zero and this page is not written to pretend otherwise. The largest remaining weakness is that no native Kannada speaker has read the lines; one native-speaker pass would change the page's standing more than any amount of additional sourcing.
